context: a letter from Hugh Falconer, which you are answering
exchanges:
You will see the Presidents address—and what he said about you and the Copley award—in this weeks ‘Reader’.

As it stands, I think you have had very fair measure of acknowledgement.

But the passage in the third Column, “on the Origin of Species”— has not been given—as it was delivered. The ‘Reader’ has left out a little sentence or two.

This will be explained to you hereafter.

With kind regards | Yours Ever | H Falconer

Many thanks for your note. I have read in the Reader Sabine’s address and was much pleased by his eulogium and glorified in the highest degree. No doubt the notice of the “Origin” was brief enough and I think it my best work; but this obscure point was hidden to me by the effulgence of the other parts! Altogether I am very much pleased. I hear from Hooker there has been some row about what Sabine exactly said. My head is whizzing like a steam engine, so no more, except once again believe that I shall ever feel grateful to you for all the extraordinary interest you have shown in my affairs.

Most sincerely yours | C. Darwin.
